overall_summary: Analysis of recent performance indicates that space and astronomy content—specifically extreme planetary 'What If' scenarios and bizarre planetary conditions—drive the highest views-per-day and engagement (likes-per-view). Videos focusing on planetary survival or mind-bending cosmic environments (e.g., Venus day/year paradox, liquid diamond planets, and extreme weather planets) significantly outperform general biology or generic psychology facts. Recent 7-day uploads are capturing strong traction, particularly formats framing extreme hypothetical questions.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,024 views) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views) show high view counts and strong like-to-view ratios compared to older static facts.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on hypothetical space disaster/immersion scenarios involving extreme planetary physics.

winning_patterns.pattern: Bizarre Cosmic Phenomenon with Counter-Intuitive Metrics
winning_patterns.evidence: 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (968 views) and 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (1,026 views) demonstrate massive engagement for short 19-21s durations.
winning_patterns.action: Maintain short, punchy 19-21 second runtimes focusing on mind-bending space oddities with startling comparative statistics.

weak_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (5 views) and 'Your Brain Is Hiding This From You' (38 views) show very poor traction and low engagement.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize psychological tricks and standard brain-teaser formats unless they feature a highly cinematic or high-stakes narrative element.

weak_patterns.evidence: Simple animal trivia like 'The Only Animal That Can Live Forever' (69 views) underperform relative to complex space and universe-scale hooks.
weak_patterns.action: Shift animal content away from static trivia toward high-stakes cinematic survival storytelling.
